title: AuthN/AuthZ Evidence Provisioning & KMS Onboarding Guidelines (signoff protocol)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce a prescriptive signoff protocol and evidence checklist to onboard enterprise customers to Redwood Private with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), SSO/SAML federation, role-based authorization, and audit log requirements. Scope includes documentation artifacts required for customer acceptance, automated evidence exports where feasible, operator runbook snippets, and a minimal set of integration tests that validate assertions used in compliance reviews.

Out of scope: deep HSM operator tooling (handled by infra-ops), legal contract language, and network-level hardening beyond documented connectivity checks. This ticket consolidates stakeholder requirements, defines acceptance artifacts, and captures the handoff steps for Customer Success and Security to sign customer enrollments as "audit-ready."
acceptance_criteria:
1) Confluence 'Onboarding Evidence Package' doc created with a checklist mapping each control to an evidence artifact (SAML metadata, KMS key policy snapshot, RBAC role bindings export, audit-log retention proof).
2) Automated evidence export script that produces a ZIP containing required files for a given customer deployment (script path and sample output attached).
3) Operator runbook additions created: key rotation verification steps, emergency key-escrow procedure, SAML assertion validation, and RBAC permission audit commands.
4) Two end-to-end smoke tests in CI that validate: (a) SAML login flow for a federated identity, (b) KMS sign/encrypt API acceptance with HSM-backed key and rotation check.
5) Security review comments resolved and signoff from Security lead recorded as a timestamped approval in the document.
6) Customer Success checklist enumerated and linked; at least one pilot customer onboarding completed using the protocol with no critical exceptions.

notes: 2026-01-22: Kickoff — stakeholders: Security (R. Alvarez), Customer Success (M. O'Neil), Infra (P. Gupta). Agreed to centralize artifacts under a single Confluence page.
2026-01-29: Decided to require KMS key policy snapshot and HSM attestation report (if available) as part of evidence package; HSM attestation may be 'deferred' for small customers where HSM not used.

2026-02-05: Eng clarified automation constraints: we can export RBAC bindings and SAML metadata, but audit-log retention proof requires sampling from the logging backend (Elastic). Marked as 'best-effort' automated export, full export via support request.
2026-02-12: Draft evidence-export script created (branch: feature/evidence-export). Current output includes: saml-metadata.xml, rbac-bindings.json, kms-policy.json, sample-audit-snapshot.ndjson
2026-02-20: Security review meeting notes: require proof of key rotation window and signed key-rotation events in audit logs. Action: add rotation verification step to smoke tests.
2026-02-25: Customer Success ran pilot with AcmeCorp; found missing newline in RBAC export causing CSV ingestion failure. Fixed in PR #487.
decisions: Require export of SAML IdP metadata and service-provider (SP) metadata for all federated customers.
Mandate KMS key policy snapshot for any customer-managed key; if HSM-backed, request vendor attestation where available but allow manual upload path.
RBAC evidence will be an export of role->principal bindings plus a 'least-privilege' deviation note produced by a simple lint rule (non-blocking for signoff).
Audit log evidence: automated sample export of last 7 days for smoke validation; full retention proof provided via logging policy doc and retention settings screenshot.
review_feedback: R. Alvarez (Security): 'Add explicit criteria for key compromise simulation and verify detection via alerting rules. Also confirm log integrity checks (SHA256) are captured.'
M. O'Neil (Customer Success): 'Customer-facing checklist needs simpler language and a one-page summary PDF for customers to sign-off on; CS will produce an annotated template.'
P. Gupta (Infra): 'HSM attestation ingestion will be manual initially; create secure upload endpoint for attestation documents and track in evidence package.'
E. Nakamura (Legal): 'Ensure evidence package includes a signed statement of data handling responsibilities; Legal will provide templated wording.'
